title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks
notes: Included for its replication history. Antoniou et al. (2019) documented MAML's training instability, and Raghu et al. (2020) found most of its benefit comes from feature reuse rather than rapid adaptation. Two claims here are annotated as not_consistent_at_reduced_scale on that basis: at small scale and few seeds, MAML's reported advantage over a well-tuned baseline is often absent or reversed, and the agent should be able to say so.

claims.text: MAML reaches higher few-shot classification accuracy on Omniglot than a network trained from scratch on the same few examples.
claims.notes: Omniglot is small and freely available; the comparison against training from scratch is a large effect.

claims.text: MAML outperforms a pretrained network that is simply fine-tuned on the few-shot task.
claims.notes: Later work found a well-tuned fine-tuning baseline matches or beats MAML, and that most of MAML's benefit is feature reuse. At reduced scale the fine-tuning baseline should hold its own, so a correct run should contradict this.

claims.text: The benefit of MAML comes from learning an initialisation that adapts rapidly, rather than from learning good reusable features.
claims.notes: Raghu et al. (2020) showed freezing the body and adapting only the head performs comparably, which contradicts the rapid-adaptation account. Testable by comparing full adaptation against head-only adaptation.

claims.text: First-order MAML performs comparably to full second-order MAML while being cheaper.
claims.notes: A claim of near-equivalence, which reduced-scale testing reports as inconclusive.

claims.text: MAML reaches 98.7% accuracy on 5-way 1-shot Omniglot classification.
MAML improves returns on continuous-control reinforcement learning tasks compared to a randomly initialised policy.
claims.notes: Requires a MuJoCo-style simulator; reinforcement learning returns are also far too noisy for three seeds.

claims.text: More gradient steps at adaptation time continue to improve MAML's performance beyond the number used during training.
claims.notes: A trend over adaptation steps; measurable but noisy at small scale.
